questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, the most important factors were the location and the opportunity to experience a new culture.  I had always wanted to experience living in Australia, and Sydney seemed like an exciting city with a lot to offer both academically and socially. UNSW also had relevant courses within public health, which was important for making the exchange fit into my degree.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UNSW provided us with the necessary information via email, where I had to follow their step-by-step guide. They also have a website where you can find a lot of useful information. Overall, it was easy to find information needed. If I had any further questions I reached out to UNSW by email and recieved a quick response.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really use any of their services when arriving in Sydney. I know they have a pick-up service in the airport, but as I travelled with my friend, I weren't in the need of any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Before the term starts, they had an orientation-week, but I didn't really participate as I where too late to sign up for their international welcoming event. There where a lot of events and activities you could attend though.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I really recommend finding long-term housing once you are physically in Sydney. Finding housing in Sydney is generally not the easiest, and it can also be quite expensive, but it is not impossible, so trust the process. My friend and I booked a temporary Airbnb for two weeks before leaving Denmark. During those two weeks, we searched for long-term housing, and we were lucky to find a nice share house through a Facebook post. Before signing up for any long-term housing, I really recommend inspecting the house in person first, to avoid scammers and pictures of the accommodation can sometimes be misleading too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was quite satisfied with living off campus actually. As UNSW dosen't have a lot of on campus options for exchange students, it was ideal for me to live off campus. In that way you can also choose whether you want to live in the inner city (CBD) or near the coast. I personally lived 30 min by public transport from UNSW and it wasn't a problem at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
To be honest, housing prices are very high, which can make it difficult to find affordable accommodation. This is just something you have to be prepared for before arriving.

UNSW also offers an online meeting before arrival, where they provide guidance on accommodation. I attended this meeting myself, and it gave me a good overview of what to look for when searching for housing and which platforms to use. I can really recommend attending this meeting. UNSW also offers personal support and guidance if needed. I did not use this service myself, but it was nice to know that the option was available.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not satisfied with the registration process at UNSW. I found their registration platform quite complicated to navigate, and the approval process took too long. To be honest, I found the whole process quite stressful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you get your accecptance letter from UNSW, you will have start the course registration. First, you need to receive pre-approval from KU, which also can be a long process. I strongly recommend that you start looking at courses in great advance. At UNSW website you can find a listing of courses. As soon as you get your pre-approval from KU, you can start registrering at UNSW. The whole course registration process ended up being very last-minute for me. I did not have my courses fully sorted out until I was already in Sydney. So I really recommend staying calm and trusting the process, even though it can feel very frustrating at times.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I used their email support a lot and contacted them whenever I had questions. I really recommend reaching out to the different services available and not hesitating to contact them if you need help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first, my courses were rejected by UNSW because, on paper, I was not yet enrolled in my master’s degree due to having postponed some courses from my bachelor’s degree. Therefore, I was also waiting for confirmation of my enrolment from KU. This was, of course, a quite specific situation and will probably not apply to everyone. I struggled a lot with this process and was in contact with both KU and UNSW. UNSW asked me to provide additional information about my situation, and in the end, they approved my courses. However, the whole process was very stressful and time-consuming.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My best advice is to start the process well in advance. Make sure you are aware of all deadlines and reach out if you need any help. From what I have heard from many other students, the course registration process can be one of the most complicated and frustrating parts of the exchange process. However, it usually works out in the end. So again, try to trust the process, even when it feels stressful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I can only speak from my own experience with the courses I chose, but my impression is that the academic level is slightly easier than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many of my courses were assessed through assignments such as reports and essays, which is a somewhat different form of assessment compared to what I am used to at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I was enrolled in the following courses in term 1 and term 2: 

Term 1 
PHCM9471-Comparative Health Care Systems
PHCM9626-Inequalities, Inequities and Health

Term 2 
PHCM9784-Communicable Disease Control in Global Health
PHCM9662-Health Aspects of Crises, Emergencies and Disasters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I particularly enjoyed the "Inequalities, Inequities and Health" course and "Comparative Health Care Systems". These courses covered some of the topics and concepts that we had already been introduced to during the bachelor’s degree in Public Health at KU. However, what made them more interesting was the international perspective and the opportunity to learn about other health systems, such as the Australian healthcare system.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In general, you will probably spent more money than you expect. I probably spent more on food than I had anticipated, mostly because you tend to eat out more often. There are also so many things to experience just in Sydney, so I would definitely recommend setting aside money for activities and experiences as well. I also travelled while I was there, which is of course another expense to keep in mind.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I spent more money on travelling than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really attend in any of their activities, so it is hard for me to tell.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! Whether you are interested in sports, cultural activities, or social events, there are many opportunities to get involved at UNSW. They offer a wide range of student clubs, societies, events, and activities throughout the term.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go travelling! Australia is such an amazing country, and I really recommend exploring places outside Sydney as well. During my exchange, I travelled to Melbourne and New Zealand, and I also did a road trip along the east coast.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Look out for activities around the city, because there is always a lot going on in Sydney! I also really recommend doing some coastal walks. Personally, I loved the Bondi to Coogee Beach Walk and the Rose Bay to Watsons Bay Walk. Sydney has so many amazing beaches that are definitely worth exploring. I also recommend renting a car and driving to the Blue Mountains. It is around a 1.5-hour drive or about 2 hours by train. The area is beautiful, and you should definitely do some hiking while you are there. I especially recommend the Grand Canyon Track.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The locals are amazing and so friendly in generel.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Personally, I did not end up socialising with many local students, as it can be a little difficult to find them. Most of the people I ended up spending time with were other exchange students from all over the world. Of course, there are also a lot of Danish people in Sydney, which is nice, but I really recommend expanding your social circle and getting to know people from different countries. For me, that was a big part of the exchange experience and made my time in Sydney even more memorable.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate australians and how open and polite they are. They love small talking, which I found really nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient with all the registration process! Even if things feel uncertain, they usually work out in the end. Just start early and keep track of deadlines. 

2. Find long-term accommodation after arriving in Sydney if possible

3. Make the most of being in Australia. Explore Sydney, travel outside the city, join activities, and meet people from different countries. There is so much to experience, and for me this was one of the best parts of the exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, everything is said.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the experiences and the people that I have met along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I cannot really point out one specific thing that was the biggest challenge. I think something that can sometimes be difficult is accepting that it is okay to do things alone and not always have plans. It is also completely normal to miss your family and friends back home. Actually, the most challenging part for me was not during the exchange itself, but all the administrative work before going.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it, because the time goes by way too fast! It is worth all the money and a once in a life time experience!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
